scope: Separately authored factual counterexamples for the explicitly pictured classroom models. Editorial regression expectations, no independent expert or empirical approval.
cases: A screwdriver rotates about its long axis; omitting this can make it an invalid false answer.
A seesaw pivots around its support.
The pictured seesaw tilts; its intended use is not a full rotation.
A lamp uses electrical energy; it is not the circuit's electrical supply.
The navigation device is not the pictured tool for collecting iron.
The oak takes up soil water through its roots; both tree and roots must count.
A mushroom remains a non-plant even though it grows.
Adult butterfly: six legs and three main body sections.
A bee also has a pupal stage, not only a butterfly.
Tadpole development is not a pupal stage.
An earthworm has no internal bony skeleton.
At the specified 20 degrees Celsius ordinary ice is not the stable solid sample.
Here metal explicitly denotes a piece of iron, not all metals.
Ordinary clear glass is not attracted like iron by the classroom magnet.
The stated fabric sample is cotton; this does not classify every textile.
Wet paper may fall apart into fibres without molecularly dissolving.
The specified ordinary oil forms a separate upper liquid layer on water.
Heart pumps blood; lungs perform the described air-to-blood oxygen transfer.
Lungs are not the pump that circulates blood.
The brain is inside the head.
The pictured tooth is a structure in the mouth.
Visible moonlight is reflected sunlight, not the Moon's own visible emission.
A physical star produces its own light; the five-point icon is a symbol.
Low precipitation defines this model, not necessarily high temperature.
Floating cloud droplets are distinguished from falling precipitation.
A paper map does not contain the compass's magnetic needle.
